objective: Make the Kernel event store the one SQLite implementation in the runtime path by widening it to multi-run per-run sequencing, and reduce the World Model store to a typed adapter over it, so there is one schema, one transaction path, one checkpoint model and one recovery procedure to maintain.
decision_supported: Whether a stored run's events can be appended, checkpointed, replayed and restored through a single SQLite implementation, and whether a multi-run database preserves per-run ordering without imposing global sequence uniqueness.
acceptance: runtime callers persist through one SQLite schema and transaction implementation, and the World Model store is an adapter over it rather than a second implementation
the World Model public call sites keep a small typed WorldEvent append/get/list/replay API
an exact retry is idempotent while a conflicting event_id or a conflicting per-run sequence_no fails visibly
one database holds several runs, each with its own contiguous sequence starting at zero, without global sequence uniqueness
checkpoint replay is defined per run and survives closing and reopening the store
an existing single-run or legacy World Model database is refused with an actionable recovery instruction rather than silently read as an empty database
integrity checking, backup and restore, and close and context-manager behaviour keep working on the single implementation
the duplicated table definition and connection lifecycle are deleted from the World Model module after the adapter's compatibility tests pass
evidence: pytest transcript for the kernel and world-model store suites with the passed count
a multi-run database transcript showing two runs whose sequences both start at zero in one file
a restart transcript showing a per-run checkpoint surviving close and reopen
a legacy-database transcript showing the migration-required diagnostic and its exit status
the full-suite transcript, the demo-scripted transcript, and ruff output
stop_conditions: the change would require editing robot/control/** or firmware/**, which is AI-write-forbidden
the change would require a contract amendment to libs/contracts or interfaces/, which needs three human approvals
the change would require adding a runtime dependency or importing ROS, Gazebo, MoveIt or a hardware SDK
the change would require changing what a WorldEvent or an event payload means, rather than how it is persisted
the change would require silently accepting an existing database whose schema cannot be proven compatible
the change would require reinterpreting an existing stored run directory rather than failing it with an actionable instruction
data_classification: public repository source, documentation and test fixtures; no secrets, personal data, credentials or physical measurement data
model_policy: AI may widen the Kernel store to multi-run sequencing, write the World Model adapter and update the affected tests; a named human Owner accepts the schema version bump and the legacy-database refusal policy
risks_and_fallbacks: widening the Kernel store from single-run to multi-run changes its validation contract; fallback is that per-run contiguity is still enforced exactly as strictly as the old whole-file contiguity, and a test asserts that an out-of-order per-run sequence is still refused

an existing Kernel or World Model database would be unreadable under the new schema; fallback is a schema-version refusal that names the old version, the new version and the recovery command, never a silent empty read
the adapter could drift from the Kernel semantics it delegates to; fallback is that the adapter owns no SQL, and a test drives the same conflict and idempotency cases through both entry points
a per-run checkpoint could be mistaken for a global one; fallback is that a checkpoint records the run it belongs to and replaying it without that run is refused
rollback is a revert of this commit; the World Model table is recreated by the previous implementation on first open, and no committed fixture or generated artifact changes
